statement: For T≥1 and ε>0, the critical-line sixth moment on [0,T] is ≪ε T^(37/30+ε).
verification: Whole-work Level 1, with endpoint arithmetic checked independently.

statement: For T^(7/60)≤V≤T^(5/38), the maximal cardinality of a 1-spaced zeta level set at threshold V on [T,2T] is ≪ε T^(24/17+ε)V^(-128/17).
For T≥1 and ε>0, the critical-line twelfth moment on [0,T] is ≪ε T^(2−520/445121+ε).
hypotheses: Unconditional. Proof uses Theorem 9.1 with auxiliary k=6, Trudgian–Yang 2025 exponent pair (64/135,122/243), and Bourgain subconvexity.

statement: For fixed k>0 and V(T)~k log log T, the normalized measure of t in [T,2T] with log|ζ(1/2+it)|>V is at most exp(exp(ck)) exp(−V²/log log T)/sqrt(log log T) for sufficiently large T and an absolute c>0.
For k≥2 the normalized critical-line 2k-th moment on [T,2T] is ≪ exp(exp(ck))(log T)^(k²) for sufficiently large T with c as in Theorem 1.1.
For every positive integer k, the partial sums of the Dirichlet coefficients μ_k of ζ(s)^(-k) satisfy |Σ_{n≤x} μ_k(n)| ≪ sqrt(x) exp(C_k (log x/log log x)^(k/(k+1))).
hypotheses: Riemann hypothesis; C_k>0. At k=1 this bounds the ordinary Mertens function.
verification: Complete primary Level 1. Scoped reconstruction of the k=1 vertical-contour estimate and central scale in audits/bui_florea_heycock_latest62_fullsource_round5.md. Cited pointwise estimates and the complete theorem proof not fully audited.
